page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.4-64 is a virtual machine instance engineered for workloads demanding higher memory allocations per compute thread. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance operates at a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled to deliver 8 vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio.

Hardware capabilities rely entirely on remote block volumes for persistent data needs, as the instance includes no local NVMe storage. Accelerator hardware is also absent, with zero GPUs present. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high RAM density relative to compute allocation provides economical provisioning for memory-heavy services without incurring the expense of unneeded processing cores, though disk-intensive workflows require careful planning around external storage attachments.

The 8 GB of RAM per vCPU positions this instance for applications that exceed typical general-purpose memory requirements. Primary workload targets include in-memory caches, distributed memory stores, mid-sized relational database systems, ETL data pipelines, and analytical batch-processing jobs that do not require specialized matrix acceleration.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.4-64 is a flexible x86_64 virtual server designed for workloads that require expanded system memory relative to compute capacity. Running on an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor at 3.9 GHz, the instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores capable of simultaneous multithreading, delivering 8 vCPUs matched with 64.0 GB of memory. It features no integrated local storage or GPU acceleration, requiring reliance on networked storage volumes for persistent data handling. Networking provisions include one complimentary public IPv4 address. By pairing a high memory volume of 8 GB per vCPU with dedicated compute cycles, the instance offers balanced resource utilization for applications where memory constraints typically dictate scaling decisions. Operational fits include caching layers, relational database servers, enterprise backend services, memory-bound ETL tasks, and analytical data workloads.
